title: KV cache precision staging and granular fallbacks
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Objective: Evaluate and produce an operational staging plan for mixed-precision KV cache serving that balances unit-cost reduction with minimal quality regression across short and long context workloads.

Background: Prior calibration work explored bulk INT8 and FP8 mappings for attention KV tensors. Those runs documented throughput gains but left gaps around long-context fidelity and tail latency under heterogeneous traffic. This ticket consolidates a set of controlled experiments, formal accuracy validations, and a staged rollout with fine-grain fallback rules (per-route and per-context-length) to enable safe production adoption.

Scope: (1) define experiment matrix covering model variants and workloads, (2) run systematic A/B and holdout validation against quality suites, (3) quantify latency/throughput/cost trade-offs, (4) produce an operator-friendly fallback policy and CI checks for runtime drift, (5) instrument dashboards and an automated rollback trigger.

Out of scope: full quantization pipeline rewrite and model-retraining flows — this ticket focuses on inference-side precision selection and operational controls.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end experiment matrix executed for 3 representative models (m-small, m-medium, m-large) on A100 and H100 hardware
Quality validation shows max average answer-similarity drop <= 2% on short-context workload and <= 3% on production-weighted mix after applying fallbacks
Latency p95 remains within -10% to +5% of current FP16 baseline for targeted routes under default traffic profiles
Documented rollout plan with per-route precision policy and automated rollback thresholds checked into runtime config repo
Dashboards (token-cost, p50/p95 latency, similarity regression metric) created and linked in this ticket
experiments: Exp A - baseline: FP16 KV for all layers. HW: A100 80GB; datasets: short-chat (<=512 tokens), long-dialog (>=4096 tokens), retrieval-augmented queries (avg 1024 tokens). Metrics: p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, cost-per-token, perplexity, answer-similarity (embedding cosine), BLEU/ROUGE where applicable.
Exp B - full INT8 KV: symmetric per-tensor INT8 using offline calibration on openwebtext+internal samples. Same HW/datasets as Exp A. Collect drift by context length bucket.
Exp C - full FP8 KV (E4M3-style dynamic scaling): single-pass calibration with per-layer scale factors and outlier clamping. Observe arithmetic stability for long contexts.
Exp D - hybrid per-layer mapping: INT8 for KV layers 0..N1, FP8 for layers N1+1..L (sensitivity-guided). Run sweeping N1 in {6,12,18} to find knee point.
Exp E - runtime-stage policies: dynamically switch to higher precision (FP16) for requests matching heuristics (long context, low-confidence embs) and evaluate cost/quality delta.
Exp F - robustness: adversarial prompts and repeated generation to detect accumulation error under INT8 for multi-turn generation.
Instrumentation: each experiment captures tags for model, kernel version, cuda/cuDNN driver, and runtime flags; results exported to perf-dashboard and qa-safety-report.
results_summary:
Summary of the primary findings from the sweep (selected highlights):

- Cost: Full INT8 reduced estimated token-compute cost by ~41% vs FP16 baseline; full FP8 reduced cost by ~27%. Hybrid mappings landed between 30-38% depending on split point.
- Latency: For common short-context traffic (<=512 tokens) INT8 p95 improved ~12% vs FP16; FP8 improved ~6%. On long-context (>=4096 tokens) INT8 p95 showed increased tail variance (p95 up to +9% vs FP16) for some kernels; FP8 maintained near-baseline p95 (+2-3%).
- Quality: Short-context answer-similarity (cosine) fell by 1.2% (INT8) and 0.5% (FP8) on average. Long-context failure modes amplified the gap: INT8 similarity drop averaged 5.6% with measurable hallucination increase on retrieval-augmented prompts; FP8 drop averaged 1.1%.
- Hybrid: best tradeoffs observed with INT8 on lower KV layers (0..11) and FP8 on upper layers. That split kept short-context similarity within 1.0% and long-context within 2.2% while preserving ~34% cost savings.
- Robustness: INT8 accumulative error surfaced primarily on repeated-attention sequences and specific outlier heads; applying per-head clamping and occasional FP16 fallback mitigated most regressions.

Conclusion: A staged rollout using the hybrid per-layer mapping plus runtime heuristics (context-length and low-confidence detection) gives the best cost-quality-latency balance for our immediate production routes. Full-int8 is still useful for low-sensitivity routes (embeddings-only, reranking) where quality requirements are lax.
decisions: Adopt a hybrid per-layer precision default: INT8 for layers 0..11, FP8 for layers 12+ for m-medium; parametrize split point per model size.
Implement runtime precision switches: promote FP16 for requests with context > 2048 tokens or when embedding-similarity confidence < 0.88.
Add per-head outlier clamp and a lightweight shadow-validation that compares sampled responses between production mapping and FP16 baseline for drift detection.
Expose a per-route flag so product teams can opt into conservative (FP8/FP16 prefer) or aggressive (INT8-first) policies.
Require a canary period with 2% of traffic and automated rollback triggers on similarity drop >2% or p95 latency increase >10% vs baseline.
Defer full automatic calibration tooling refactor to separate ticket — this work uses existing offline calibration scripts with some added automation for sample selection.
next_steps: Merge PR with runtime config schema for per-route precision policy and fallback thresholds (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1298)
Schedule canary rollout for route 'chat-default' at 2% traffic for 72h and monitor dashboards
Add unit tests and integration test that run sampled prompts in CI shadow-validation against FP16 baseline
Create runbook entries for ops: how to interpret similarity/latency dashboards and execute immediate rollback
Open follow-up ticket to extend per-head clamping logic (ENG-37121) and to add automated calibration sweep infra (ENG-37122)
